newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco sells $47.2 million of bonds.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco sells $47.2 million of bonds.

text.p: San Francisco sold $47.2 million of general obligation bonds, Mayor Willie Brown announced on Monday.
The bonds outperformed the municipal bond market by 0.13 percent, according to the mayor's office.
"This exceptional performance will result in a savings of about 2 percent, or $1 million, to the city's property tax payers over the life of the bonds," Brown said.
The bonds are 20-year bonds bearing fixed rates of interest and are repaid from property tax receipts. Proceeds will be used to improve schools and Golden Gate Park.
